title: Quarterly milestone lattice: coordinated roadmap & gating for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Goal: Create an operationalizable quarterly roadmap artifact (the 'milestone lattice') that maps Hosted API product features and model catalog changes to deterministic decision gates, evaluation triggers, and rollout windows so Engineering, Research, Console, and GTM teams can coordinate with clear SLAs and rollback criteria.

Context: Previous quarters used a mix of slide decks and ad-hoc PRDs which made it hard to synchronize canaries across model rotations and endpoint changes. This ticket produces one canonical roadmap + gating matrix for the quarter covering: model onboarding, variant rotation, canary windows, performance/regression gates, and contingency lanes.

Deliverables: 
- Milestone lattice doc (single Confluence page) that lists milestones by week, owners, dependent systems, and a pass/fail gating checklist.
- Gating rubric with quantitative thresholds: latency P50/P95 targets, token cost delta thresholds, quality regression thresholds per eval set, and error-rate ceilings.
- Canary schedule: committed canary windows per model line (timeboxed), fallback model mappings, and automated rollback playbook.
- Stakeholder sync cadence: weekly LAUNCH-ops + biweekly cross-functional review with Research/Evals.
- Exportable CSV used by Console to render a timeline and by Eng to generate deploy windows.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Confluence milestone lattice published and shared with stakeholders.
2) Each milestone has an owner and at least one engineering contact + required test signals.
3) Gating rubric includes numeric thresholds and at least three eval prompts tied to regression alerts.
4) Canary schedule is integrated with the release calendar and Console rollout API (tickets to Eng-owned feature flags created).

Trade-offs considered: 
- Aggressive model freshness (faster rotations) increases eval overhead and false positives on regressions. We propose a three-lane approach (fast-rotation experimental lane, standard lane, and long-stable lane) to balance freshness and reliability.
- Cost vs latency: some models exceed token-cost thresholds; gating includes a per-customer cost-impact flag so revenue-sensitive endpoints can opt into slower rollouts.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Canary failures during peak traffic. Mitigation: schedule major canaries during low-traffic windows and ensure automated rollback paths + secondary region fallback.
- Risk: Incomplete eval coverage. Mitigation: require minimum eval sets per model and create a 'hold' state for models without complete coverage.

Notes for Console/Engineering: the CSV schema will include: milestone_id, start_date, end_date, model_tag, owner, gating_thresholds (encoded), fallback_model, release_window_id. Engineering owners: tag Eng-ops and Runtime leads in the Confluence doc for runbook handoff.
